_what: The UploadFile request and response as the PAGE actually makes them, captured with a listener attached. Data, so a probe cannot invent the shape and a disagreement is visible instead of argued about.
_supersedes: A first version of this file, transcribed on 2026-09-18 from a 400-character truncated body_head in a 2026-09-17 CDP recording. It listed THREE fields and missed optionsSets entirely, and a test was then written to pin agreement with it -- a guard holding a probe to an incomplete record. Anything built against that version would have been wrong again in a new way. A truncated observation is not an observation of the whole.

fields.name: conversationId
fields.note: A REAL conversation the page is in. The RESPONSE echoes one back, which is how the id can be tied to a conversation.

fields.name: FileBase64
fields.note: NOT a binary file part. The bytes travel as a base64 DATA URI inside an ordinary text field, prefix included.

fields.name: optionsSets
fields.note: REPEATED THREE TIMES -- the field appears three times in one body, not once with three values. Missed by the first transcription because the body was truncated at 400 characters. Values are not recorded here: they are feature flags that change with the client build, so a probe should copy them from a live capture rather than hardcode a snapshot.

auth.note: MEASURED, not assumed. The call is bearer-authenticated and sends no cookie, so 'which audience does the token need' is a well-formed question about this endpoint -- which had NOT been established when a 403 was first interpreted that way. The token value is never read or recorded.

_header_note: A probe sending only Authorization differs in far more than the credential. x-anchormailbox in particular routes the request; origin and referer are checked by many Microsoft endpoints. Values are deliberately not transcribed -- some identify the account -- so a probe must copy them from a live capture, not from this file.

response.note: CAPTURED FOR THE FIRST TIME on 2026-09-18. Before this, zero response bodies had ever been seen here, and 'the page successfully uploaded' was an inference from a POST plus a later annotation. It is now a reading: result.value == 'Success'.

docid_is_the_annotation_id.note: Same shape, so the response's docId is what rides the socket as messageAnnotations[0].id. That provenance was unproven while no response had been captured.

follow_on_frame: messageAnnotations[0] = {id, messageAnnotationMetadata: {@type: File, fileType: png, fileName}, messageAnnotationType: ImageFile}

answered_2026_09_18.question: Is the token the relay captures (audience substrate.office.com/sydney) accepted here?
answered_2026_09_18.answer: YES. The page's own request re-issued with ONLY the Authorization swapped returned 200 and result.value 'Success'.
answered_2026_09_18.how: scripts/probes/replay_upload_with_our_token.py -- it captures the page's bytes and headers and re-issues them. Two earlier probes RECONSTRUCTED the request, both got 403, and both were reported as answers about the credential. They were answers about the reconstruction: one sent a binary part named 'file', both omitted optionsSets x3, and both sent ONE header where the page sends eighteen.

what_is_still_unknown: How long a docId remains usable.

Whether an annotation carrying a docId is accepted when the frame is sent over the socket rather than by the page. A 200 from UploadFile does not answer this, and until it does an attachment still goes to a tab.

socket_annotation._question: Is an annotation carrying a docId accepted when the frame goes over the socket?

observed_2026_09_17.sent: The PAGE sent a webSocketFrameSent whose arguments[0] carried messageAnnotations[0] = {id, messageAnnotationMetadata:{@type:File, annotationType:File, fileType:png, fileName}, messageAnnotationType:ImageFile}.
observed_2026_09_17.echoed_back: The following webSocketFrameReceived carried the same id with messageAnnotationSource:'UserAnnotated' and turnCount:1.
observed_2026_09_17.reading: The server ACCEPTS an annotated frame on this socket. That is about the PAGE's send, with the page's own frame and credential -- not about ours.

why_it_is_not_enough_to_act_on: THE CAPTURED FRAME IS TRUNCATED AND THEREFORE NOT A TEMPLATE. declared len 4811, captured 4000, cut by 811 characters, and it does not parse as JSON. The recorder wrote payload[:4000]. This is the same defect as the 400-character body_head that produced three wrong UploadFile probes on 2026-09-18: a truncated observation is not an observation.

relay/chathub.py sends the CLIENT'S OWN captured template with this turn's ids and text written in, and its docstring records that a COMPOSED frame was measured REJECTED on 2026-08-20 while the captured shape was accepted (result=Success). So the annotation cannot be composed into a frame -- it has to come from a template that carries it.
No template in this repository carries messageAnnotations today.
socket_annotation.what_would_answer_it: Re-capture the page's annotated frame WITHOUT truncation (the recorder's cap must exceed the frame, which was 4811 characters here), turn it into a RequestTemplate, and send one turn through it with a docId from UploadFile written in. Producing the capture needs a real message sent WITH an attachment -- attaching alone produces the UploadFile POST but no chat frame.
socket_annotation.docid_lifetime: NOT MEASURED, and it cannot be measured before the above: 'how long does a docId stay usable' has no meaning until there is a way to use one. Two uploads of the same bytes returned different docIds (0-ejp-d1-149e4084... and 0-ejp-d1-9717cadd...), so an id is per-upload rather than per-file.
